- **What happens when you create an independently creative AI content engine and let it loose on topics from Whiskey, the Stock Market, or Fast Fashion? I set up a small project called The Cassandra Files. It generates and publishes “episodes” — each with short articles and a 20-minute podcast—across topics like Business, Health, Technology and Culture. There are over 20 episodes so far and over 100 more in the backlog. What I didn’t expect is that recurring themes and connections are starting to emerge across them—almost like a loose narrative forming over time. Still early, but it’s an interesting shift from creating content piece by piece to letting a system grow, learn and evolve. If you’re curious:**

- **If you want to build a five-trillion-dollar empire, stop feeding your employees. For the past two decades, Silicon Valley has convinced us that the secret to corporate greatness lies in the additional 'perks'. Google gave us free gourmet breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Meta showered staff with meal vouchers. We were told that corporate culture was best built in well-stocked micro-kitchens where serendipity and free snacks would spark the next multi-billion-dollar idea. Then came Nvidia. At Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, employees pay for their own lunch. The coffee might be free, but the snacks and bottled drinks come out of your own pocket. It sounds like a corporate misstep, a bizarre piece of penny-pinching from a business fueling the global artificial intelligence boom. Yet, while other tech giants are quietly clawing back their perks and policing meal voucher abuse, Nvidia boasts an astonishing employee turnover rate of just 3.7%. The semiconductor industry average sits closer to 17%. How do you keep people working through gruelling seven-day weeks and late-night shifts without free sushi? You give them a piece of the rocket ship. As Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, says himself, "When you take care of people, everything else takes care of itself." By offering a remarkably generous employee stock purchase plan alongside deep equity incentives, Nvidia now boasts that an estimated 75% of its workers are millionaires. Nearly half are worth more than 25 million dollars. It turns out that employees do not actually want a free avocado toast station. They want to be valued, do meaningful work, and have an actual stake in the future they are building.**

- **A week before I started at Bristol Myers Squibb in 2022 my brother-in-law passed away from pancreatic cancer, leaving my sister-in-law and four nieces behind. Seeing him fight this disease with incredible strength until the last day, left a mark on me. When I first heard about #C2C4C (country to country for cancer) and the quest to support Initiative Krebskranke Kinder München, e.V. in its mission to support children affected by cancer, I knew that one day I had to participate. I’m honored to be a 2026 C2C4C rider and I’m riding in memory of my brother-in-law Amador. Amador was an avid road cyclist, so there is no better way to honor his memory than by cycling 360km to support children affected by cancer. Every Euro counts and I’m thankful for your contribution! #BMS_employee #C2C4C Donate here: https://lnkd.in/etrV4WQz**
